To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the InAs/InGaAs quantum dots grown on InP (113) substrate are a promising candidate for the realization of high performance mode-locked lasers operating at telecom wavelengths.

(1) We have demonstrated a self-starting mode-locked operation at 1.58µm with 1.5ps pulse width for the first time in InAs QD lasers on (113) B InP substrates; (2) A RF spectral width of 20kHz has been obtained leading a low timing jitter of 1.3 ps RMS.
we demonstrate the first passive mode locking of InAs/InGaAs QDs grown on (113B) InP substrates emitting at 1.58µm with repetition rates of 23GHz and 39GHz and with pulse durations down to 1ps.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the realization of mode-locked semiconductor lasers with repetition rates of a few tens of GHz.
the development of high performance InAs/InGaAs QD lasers emitting at telecommunication wavelength.
the development of high-speed InAs QDs mode-locked lasers emitting around 1 µm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of (113)B substrate for QD lasers has allowed to demonstrate for the first time the mode-locking of InAs/Inp quantum dot laser.
the use of InAs QDs on (113) B InP substrates is a promising way to obtain high speed mode-locked lasers with low phase noise.

the (113)B substrate has been demonstrated to be a viable option to grow QD structures with good optical and electrical properties and, at the same time, to be a good candidate to realize high performance mode locked lasers in the 1.3 µm wavelength range.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the InAs/Inp quantum dot lasers are very promising for high repetition rate pulse generation.
the QDs (113)B lasers are a promising candidate for future high repetition rate mode-locking lasers.
the InAs/InGaAs/InP quantum-dot (QD) lasers are promising candidates for the development of compact, low-cost, and low power-consumption sources of ultra-short optical pulses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
InAs quantum dots grown on (113)-oriented InP substrate can be used for the fabrication of high repetition rate mode-locked lasers with low phase noise and high stability.
the InAs/InAlAs/InP QD material system is a promising candidate for the realization of low phase noise, high repetition rate, monolithic mode-locked lasers.
InAs QDs grown on (113)-oriented InP substrate are a viable alternative to the InAs QDs on (001)-oriented InP for mode-locking applications.
